answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Auditors are sampled from agents with their own bonded deposits, so inventing a meadow of fake identities does not create free voting power: each one needs capital at risk. A beacon can announce audit challenges, while the forge of fabricated accounts becomes costly because the attacker must fund every stake and may lose it when caught.
